name: Stonehenge & Salisbury
description: Visit the iconic 5,000-year-old stone circle, one of the world's most famous prehistoric monuments. Combine it with the medieval city of Salisbury, home to a magnificent cathedral with the tallest spire in England and one of four surviving copies of the Magna Carta.
travelTime: 1h 30min by train to Salisbury, then bus to Stonehenge
tips: Book a morning visit to avoid crowds. The visitor centre exhibition is excellent and included in the ticket price.

name: Windsor Castle
description: Explore the oldest and largest occupied castle in the world, an official residence of the King. The State Apartments are lavishly furnished, and St George's Chapel is the resting place of Queen Elizabeth II and other monarchs.
travelFrom: London Paddington (change at Slough) or London Waterloo
tips: Check the Changing of the Guard schedule online before you go — it doesn't happen every day. Arrive early to get a good viewing spot.

name: Oxford
description: The 'City of Dreaming Spires' is home to the world's oldest English-speaking university, with 38 colleges spread across the city. Wander through ancient quads, visit the Bodleian Library, and punt on the River Cherwell.
tips: Christ Church College was used as a filming location for Harry Potter. Visit the Covered Market for lunch — it's been trading since 1774.

name: Cambridge
description: Cambridge rivals Oxford with its stunning university colleges, world-class museums, and peaceful riverside setting. Punting along the River Cam past the iconic 'Backs' of the colleges is an unmissable experience.
tips: Shared punting tours are cheaper than hiring your own punt, and the guides tell great stories. Visit during term time to see the colleges at their liveliest.

name: Brighton
description: London's favourite seaside escape combines a pebbly beach, vibrant street art in the North Laine, the exotic Royal Pavilion palace, and a legendary nightlife scene. Perfect for a fun, relaxed day out by the sea.
tips: Get fish and chips from one of the seafront shops and eat on the beach. If the weather is good, walk along the coast towards the Marina.

name: Warner Bros Harry Potter Studio Tour
description: Step into the Wizarding World at the original studios where all eight Harry Potter films were made. Walk through the Great Hall, explore Diagon Alley, and see real props, costumes, and sets including the Hogwarts Express.
tips: Book tickets well in advance — they sell out weeks ahead. Allow at least 3.5 hours for the tour. The shuttle bus from Watford Junction runs frequently.

name: Bath
description: A UNESCO World Heritage city famed for its elegant Georgian architecture, ancient Roman baths, and the stunning Royal Crescent. Bath is one of England's most beautiful cities, with Jane Austen connections and excellent restaurants.
tips: The Thermae Bath Spa has a rooftop pool with city views — perfect for relaxing. Grab a Sally Lunn bun from the oldest house in Bath.

name: Canterbury
description: This ancient pilgrimage city centres on the magnificent Canterbury Cathedral, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the seat of the Church of England. Wander medieval streets, explore Roman ruins, and enjoy the charming historic centre.
tips: The high-speed train from St Pancras is much faster than alternatives. Visit Tiny Tim's Tearoom for a proper English cream tea.

name: Stratford-upon-Avon
description: The birthplace of William Shakespeare is a charming Tudor market town on the River Avon. Visit Shakespeare's Birthplace, see a play at the Royal Shakespeare Company theatre, and stroll along the picturesque riverbank.
tips: Book RSC matinee tickets in advance for a once-in-a-lifetime theatre experience. A combined ticket for all five Shakespeare family houses saves money.

name: Hampton Court Palace
description: Henry VIII's magnificent Tudor palace sits on the banks of the Thames with spectacular gardens, a famous maze, and 500 years of royal history. The palace kitchens and the Hampton Court Maze are highlights not to miss.
tips: Allow at least half a day — the palace and gardens are vast. The Magic Garden play area is brilliant for children under 12.

name: Leeds Castle
description: Often called the 'loveliest castle in the world', Leeds Castle sits on two islands in a lake surrounded by 500 acres of parkland in Kent. With a maze, grotto, falconry displays, and beautiful interiors, it makes for a wonderful day out.
travelTime: 1h by train to Bearsted, then shuttle bus
tips: The castle shuttle bus runs from Bearsted station. Pack a picnic to enjoy by the lake — there are also cafes on site.

name: Blenheim Palace
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and the birthplace of Sir Winston Churchill. This monumental Baroque palace near Oxford features opulent State Rooms, 2,000 acres of Capability Brown-designed parkland, and stunning formal gardens.
travelTime: 1h 20min by train to Oxford, then bus
tips: Combine with a morning in Oxford since the bus to Blenheim departs from the city centre. The miniature train ride around the grounds is fun for kids.

name: Seven Sisters Cliffs
description: These dramatic white chalk cliffs on the East Sussex coast are even more photogenic than the White Cliffs of Dover. A walk along the cliff tops offers breathtaking views of the English Channel, rolling downland, and the iconic coastguard cottages.
travelTime: 1h 30min by train to Eastbourne or Seaford
tips: Wear sturdy shoes — the cliff-top path is uneven. The walk from Seaford to Eastbourne via the cliffs is about 10 miles. Check the tide times before descending to any beaches.

name: Greenwich (River Cruise)
description: Take a scenic Thames river cruise to historic Greenwich, home to the Prime Meridian, the Royal Observatory, the Cutty Sark, and the stunning Painted Hall. Stand with one foot in each hemisphere and enjoy sweeping views from the hilltop park.
travelTime: 30min by river cruise from Westminster Pier
tips: The river cruise itself is a highlight — sit on the top deck for the best views. Greenwich Market has great street food for lunch. The National Maritime Museum is free.

name: Kew Gardens
description: The Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew are a UNESCO World Heritage Site with over 50,000 living plants across 300 acres. Explore the iconic Victorian glasshouses, treetop walkway, Japanese garden, and the world's largest collection of living plants.
travelTime: 30min by Tube (District line to Kew Gardens station)
tips: Spring and summer are the best times to visit when everything is in bloom. The Orangery restaurant is a lovely spot for afternoon tea. Allow at least 3-4 hours.
